chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Washsha, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If he reaches his maturity, that is, completes thirteen years and enters the fourteenth – then it becomes obligatory on him what is obligatory on those who have nocturnal emissions whether he himself has emissions or not, and his sins are written down for him, and his good-deeds are also written down for him, and everything becomes permissible for him [in financial terms] except if he is mentally incapacitated or foolhardy.
ai.seo_question: What is the age of legal maturity for boys in Shia fiqh according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the age of legal maturity (bulugh) in Shia jurisprudence as the completion of thirteen lunar years and entering the fourteenth, emphasizing that religious accountability (taklif) and financial capacity are triggered by age alone, independent of physical signs like nocturnal emission. It further clarifies that this status applies provided the individual is not mentally incapacitated (safiha) or physically weak, reflecting the Shia principle that chronological age is the primary determinant for the onset of duties and rights.
